condition: Every declared unit of weight or measure must be based on the metric system (SI or units recognised under these rules); non-metric/imperial units are not legally valid.
notes: Imperial/non-metric units are outside the metric system mandated by Rule 3 and therefore non-compliant for any legal declaration of weight or measure.

condition: Base SI unit for mass declarations must be the kilogram (kg) or its permitted decimal sub/multiples formed on 'gram'.
notes: Kilogram is the SI base unit of mass.

condition: Base SI unit for length declarations must be the metre (m) or its permitted decimal sub/multiples.
Thermodynamic temperature must be expressed in kelvin (K); the degree Celsius (°C) is also permitted for expressing temperature or a temperature interval, where 0°C = 273.15 K.
The SI base unit of time is the second (s); minute, hour and day are permitted units (Fourth Schedule).
Net quantity of a liquid commodity must be declared in litre (l/L) or its decimal sub-multiple millilitre (ml/mL), or the coherent SI unit cubic metre (m3) for technical use.
Litre must NOT be used for work involving precise/legal measurements; cubic metre and its coherent SI sub-multiples must be used instead for precision measurement/calibration contexts.
example_valid: Calibration certificate expressed in m3, dm3

condition: Bulk/industrial mass declarations may use the tonne (t), equal to 1000 kg; only the SI prefixes 'kilo', 'mega', 'giga' and 'tera' may be combined with tonne.
example_invalid: Net Quantity: 25 mt (used to mean milli-tonne)

condition: The unit 'carat' (c), equal to 200 mg, may be used to declare mass ONLY for diamonds, pearls and precious stones; use for any other commodity category is not permitted.
notes: Compliance check must cross-reference declared commodity category before accepting 'carat' as valid.

field: Net Quantity Unit (Food Grain / Farm Produce)
condition: The unit 'quintal' (q), equal to 100 kg, may be used for large commercial transactions in food grain, farm produce and other consumer commodities.
Nautical mile and knot may only be used for marine and aerial navigation purposes, not for general commercial declarations.
invalid_values: nautical mile (on a general commodity label)

condition: 'Are' and 'hectare' may be used only for land measurement; SI prefixes (Third Schedule) must NOT be combined with 'are' or 'hectare'.
Kilometre per hour (km/h) is a temporarily accepted unit intended for velocity declarations (e.g., vehicles); it is not a valid unit for declaring net quantity of a packaged commodity.

Units listed in the Seventh Schedule (CGS units: erg, dyne, poise, stokes, gauss, oersted, maxwell, stilb, phot) must NOT be used for general/commercial purposes or education; permitted only for scientific and technological research, and only with their prescribed symbols.
example_invalid: Net Quantity: 500 dyn (on a commercial label)

condition: Units listed in the Eighth Schedule (fermi, torr, kilogram-force, calorie, micron, X unit, stere, gamma, lambda) must NOT be used for general/commercial purposes or education; permitted only for scientific and technological research, and only with their prescribed symbols.
example_invalid: Energy content: 250 calorie (on general commercial label instead of kcal/kJ as applicable)

condition: No new unit of weight or measure may be formed or used (other than for scientific and technological research) without the prior approval of the Central Government.
example_invalid: A proprietary/undefined unit symbol invented by a manufacturer and printed on the label

condition: Derived units listed in the Second Schedule may be used only for scientific or technological research purposes; general commercial declarations should use the corresponding Permitted/Base unit (e.g., litre instead of cubic metre) where one exists.
The unit symbol must be placed after the complete numerical value with a single space between the number and the symbol.
Unit symbols must not be pluralised (no trailing 's').
Unit symbols must not carry a trailing full stop/period unless required by normal end-of-sentence punctuation.
Unit symbols must be printed in roman (upright) type, regardless of the surrounding text style.

Unit symbols must be in lower case, except that the first letter is capitalised only when the unit is named after a person (e.g., N, Pa, Wb); everyday commodity units (g, kg, l, ml, m, cm) are always lower case.
Only one SI prefix may be used to form a multiple/sub-multiple of a compound unit; compound (stacked) prefixes are not permitted.
Decimal multiples/sub-multiples of the mass unit must be formed by attaching the SI prefix to the word 'gram', not 'kilogram'.
The letter 'p' must not be used to denote 'per'/division; a solidus (/) or negative exponent notation must be used instead.
No more than one solidus (/) may appear on the same line in a compound unit formed by division, unless parentheses are used to remove ambiguity.
The numerical value of a declared quantity should ordinarily be expressed, using an appropriate SI prefix, such that the number falls between 0.1 and 1000.
The decimal separator used in a declared numeric value must be a dot (full stop), not a comma.
Digit groups of a large number must not be separated by commas or dots; if grouped, groups of three digits are separated by a thin space only.
Alcoholic strength must be declared as '% Vol' (by volume, measured at 20°C) or '% mass' (by mass), per International Recommendation No. 22 on Alcoholometry.
Sugar content of a sugar solution may be declared as Degree Brix (°Bx) or on the International Sugar Scale (°S).
Relative humidity must be expressed as a percentage (% RH).
pH must be expressed as the base-10 logarithm of the inverse hydrogen ion concentration, reported as a plain number (no unit suffix) e.g., 'pH 6.5'.
Hardness of materials, where declared, must use a recognised scale: Brinell (HB), Vickers (HV), or Rockwell (HRB/HRC), each verified per the applicable International Recommendation.

Where a coefficient corresponds to one specified in the Tenth Schedule but uses a non-standard name/symbol, such usage is permitted only for five years from commencement of these rules (or from the date the corresponding standard coefficient was added); thereafter, use of the Tenth-Schedule name and symbol is compulsory.

Where a physical constant (e.g., speed of light, Planck constant, Avogadro constant, Boltzmann constant) is cited in a technical declaration, the numerical value and unit specified in the Ninth Schedule must be used, except for values used in research aimed at redetermining the constant itself.

Only the specific unit name/symbol combinations defined in the applicable Schedule (First to Tenth) may be used for the corresponding physical quantity; substituting an undefined symbol for a defined unit is non-compliant.

Where a commodity is customarily sold by number/count rather than by weight or measure, declaring the quantity as a count (e.g., 'pieces', 'units') is an acceptable alternative to a unit of weight or measure.
reference: Rule 2(definition of derived/base units; general scheme of the Act)
notes: This class of declaration is governed in more detail by the separate Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011.
